A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sMBR study and contain readable text, equations, three figures, fourteen tables, and Appendices A–I. The final line on v4's page 20 moves onto v5's page 19; no substantive material is missing.

before.justification: v4 reports original translation experiments, source and candidate-count analyses, generator comparisons, and timing measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the work's original translation results and supplementary analyses, including the experimental results in Tables 1–14.

M1.justification: Appendix A changes the specified paraphrase-generator encoder input from 'paraphrase: {source_text}' to '{source_text}' during training and inference. This is a limited input-specification revision; the sMBR scoring rule, model architectures, and paraphrasing/back-translation components remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training and evaluation datasets, three translation directions, classic high- and low-resource settings, and TowerInstruct-13B setting. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain MAP, QE reranking, and COMET-based MBR with the same support-set variants. Appendix comparisons involving MBR-fast, GPT-4 paraphrasing, and diverse beam search are also already present in v4.

E3.justification: Removing the task prefix in Appendix A revises a previously stated preprocessing setting for paraphrase-model training and inference. Splits, budgets, candidate counts, and evaluation metrics otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendices F–I retain the same source-count and candidate-count sweeps, quasi-source quality and QE-score analyses, efficiency measurements, GPT-4 generator comparison, and diverse-beam-search experiment.

E5.justification: Captions to Tables 1 and 6–10 now explicitly state that bootstrap comparisons cover all methods against QE reranking. This refines statistical reporting; the test type, significance thresholds, significance markers, absence of multiple-testing correction, and five-run timing averages remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All fourteen tables retain identical result entries and values, and Figure 3 retains the same plotted curves. For example, Table 1's high-resource En→De sMBR-PP scores remain XCOMET 86.73 and MetricX 3.09. Qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the paraphrasing-distribution formulation, the uniform-average approximation, the relationship to QE reranking, and Appendix F's computational-complexity reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim about using sources as MBR support hypotheses and the same performance claims relative to QE reranking and standard MBR.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning source diversity, QE sensitivity, and differences between classic and LLM results are retained. Limitations concerning metric bias, quasi-source quality, efficiency, and language coverage are unchanged.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces a future code-release promise with a model-and-code availability statement and repository link. Section 4.1.3 newly specifies that evaluations use reference translations unless stated otherwise, and Appendix A revises the input format. External availability was not verified.

R1.justification: The reference lists are identical, and the related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior MBR decoding and QE reranking research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited wording and heading edits, including 'Method' to 'Proposed Method,' updates author email addresses, corrects an appendix reference, and adds acknowledgements. The narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The figures and tables retain their organization and content, with limited caption revisions. Printed page numbers disappear, and local text reflow incorporates v4's final one-line page into page 19 without removing content.

improvement.justification: v5 provides concrete model/code access information where v4 only promised a future release, and clarifies reference use and statistical comparison scope. These changes modestly improve reproducibility information and reporting clarity. The scientific evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged, and the input-format revision does not establish a performance improvement.
